subject: AI & Agents
title: Convolutional Networks: AI That Sees
description: A micro-lesson that makes Convolutional Networks: AI That Sees usable.

hook.text: Show a CNN a photo of a cat and it detects whiskers, ears, fur patterns — all automatically.

buildup.text: Convolutional Neural Networks slide small filters across images to detect local features.

discovery.text: Pooling layers shrink the representation. Multiple conv layers detect increasingly complex patterns.

twist.text: CNNs work because visual features are local — an eye is always a small patch, not spread across pixels.

climax.text: CNNs power face recognition, medical imaging, self-driving vision, and image search.

punchline.text: Slide, detect, pool. Repeat until you see the whole picture.

quiz.question: Why do CNNs work well for images?
options: They exploit the local structure of visual features
They process text and images identically

details.summary: Convolutional neural networks process images by scanning with small filters that detect edges, textures, and shapes. Layers stack from simple features to complex objects, mirroring how biological vision works.
details.whyItMatters: CNNs are the backbone of computer vision, powering everything from medical imaging to self-driving cars. Understanding their layer-by-layer approach reveals how AI builds visual understanding.
takeaways: CNNs scan images with filters that detect visual features
Lower layers find edges; deeper layers recognize whole objects
They power most AI image recognition applications

faq.question: How does a convolutional filter work?
faq.answer: A small matrix slides across the image, computing a dot product at each position. Each filter detects a specific feature like a vertical edge or color gradient. Many filters together capture diverse visual patterns.

faq.question: Are CNNs still used now that Transformers exist?
faq.answer: Yes. CNNs remain efficient for many vision tasks, especially on devices with limited compute. Vision Transformers are powerful but computationally heavier. Many systems use hybrid CNN-Transformer designs.
